suggested_experiment_name: JWST (James Webb Space Telescope) - Dark Photon Dark Matter Detection via Haloscope
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter ε (dimensionless), as plotted on y-axis labeled 'ε × (ρ_DM / ρ_M)^0.5'
notes: This paper presents PROJECTED SENSITIVITY (not measured limits) for dark photon dark matter detection using a modified JWST configuration during ground-testing. The authors propose adjusting mirror positions in the Optical Telescope Element (OTE) to focus DPDM-induced photons onto detectors. The projected upper limits on kinetic mixing parameter ϵ are ϵ ∼ 10^−12 − 10^−14 in the frequency range 10−500 THz (corresponding to masses ~4.1e-15 eV to 2.1e-12 eV) at 95% C.L. The paper analyzes why current JWST in space cannot detect DPDM signals (photons propagate perpendicular to optical path) but argues future space telescopes could achieve these sensitivities with modified configurations during ground tests. The data points encode the stated range as a horizontal band spanning the frequency range. The local DM density of 0.3 GeV/cm³ is the standard halo model assumption used implicitly in the dark matter velocity distribution (Maxwellian with v₀ ≈ 235 km/s). This is a haloscope-type experiment searching for local DPDM conversion to photons. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 4 shows constraints on kinetic mixing parameter ε between Dark Photon Dark Matter (DPDM) and photons in the randomized polarization scheme. The plot displays multiple experimental constraints: XENON1T (orange), JWST-MIRI (red), JWST-NIR (red dashed), and comparisons with Solar, LAMPOST, FUNK, and Tokyo limits. The x-axis spans 0.05–2.0 eV in mass (converted from frequency range 10–500 THz using m[eV] = 4.136e-15 × f[Hz]). The y-axis shows ε × (ρ_DM/ρ_M)^0.5 ranging from 1e-15 to 1e-9. The lower boundary traced represents the JWST-MIRI exclusion limit, which is the most stringent JWST constraint in this mass range. The boundary shows a steep decline at low masses (10–50 THz), flattens in the mid-range (50–200 THz), and rises slightly at high masses (200–500 THz). Sampling density increased at the transition points (~50 THz and ~200 THz) where the slope changes. The dashed red curve represents projected sensitivity for a modified JWST configuration with optimized mirror positioning for DPDM detection. | Calibration: Vision calibration: ×1e-1 (factor=1.00e-01, reason=spot-check verify/stage2, raw_ratio=0.13)
